passage: Whether you're just having a down day or a down period, taking a walk can instantly lift your mood, especially when you go outdoors. Not only can walking make you less depressed, but according to a new study, depression sufferers who took a {{1}}  walk showed just as much improvement in their {{2}}  as people taking medicine. In fact, 60-70 percent of the participants in the study could no longer even be {{3}}  as depressed. Bone density may not be one of the most exciting health benefits of walking, but it's an important one. People with stronger bones avoid osteoporosis(骨质疏松症) and all the problems that {{4}}  with it, like breaks and other disabilities. And the best way to get strong, healthy bones is by doing weight-bearing exercises like running, dancing and walking, according to a large study. But as regards bones, it's  {{5}} use it or lose it: To keep your bones strong you have to keep exercising. The researchers found that adults who walked regularly had better bone density throughout their lives than their {{6}}  friends. Taking a walk can be great for {{7}}  your head or blowing off some steam. It also provides a great opportunity to  {{8}} with friends and family, far away from electronics and other {{9}}  at home. Even better, you set a powerful example because when they see you  {{10}} the benefits of walking, they'll be encouraged to walk more, too.
